references.text: The parallel passage in Matthew where the wicked servant says in his heart that the master is delaying, and begins to beat his fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards ([ref:Matt 24:48-49|Matthew 24:48-49]).

The preacher warns that when judgment against an evil deed is not executed immediately, people are emboldened to do what is evil—the same mindset as the servant who exploits the master's delay ([ref:Eccles 8:11|Ecclesiastes 8:11]).

Isaiah describes shepherds (leaders) who are preoccupied with drinking and feasting instead of caring for the flock, paralleling the unfaithful servant who eats, drinks, and gets drunk ([ref:Isa 56:12|Isaiah 56:12]).

Peter warns about scoffers who say, "Where is the promise of his coming?" and use the Lord's apparent delay as an excuse—the same attitude as the servant who says, "My master is delaying in coming" ([ref:2 Pet 3:3-4|2 Peter 3:3-4]).
The Lord does not delay with the promise, but is patient—a correction of the idea that the Lord's delay means an absence of judgment ([ref:2 Pet 3:9|2 Peter 3:9]).

The day of the Lord will come like a thief in the night, and those who say, "Peace and safety" will be struck by sudden destruction—a parallel to the unfaithful servant who did not expect the master's coming ([ref:1 Thess 5:2-3|1 Thessalonians 5:2-3]).
Jesus' warning not to let your hearts be weighed down with carousing and drunkenness, which reflects the unfaithful servant's feasting and intoxication ([ref:Luke 21:34|Luke 21:34]).
The bridegroom delayed (ἐχρόνιζεν), and the virgins fell asleep—the same motif of the master's delay as a test of faithfulness ([ref:Matt 25:5|Matthew 25:5]).

When Moses delayed in coming down from the mountain, the people gathered against Aaron and demanded idols—an Old Testament example of unfaithfulness when the leader appears to be delayed ([ref:Exod 32:1|Exodus 32:1]).
The preceding context about the faithful and wise steward who does his duty while the master is away, in contrast to the unfaithful servant in verse 45 ([ref:Luke 12:42-44|Luke 12:42-44]).
The immediate result: the master's coming on an unexpected day and hour, with severe judgment upon the unfaithful servant ([ref:Luke 12:46|Luke 12:46]).
